body.x: Faraday Dynamics Inc. participated in the CES 2026 HUMANOID M.AX Alliance joint pavilion, held in Las Vegas, the United States, from January 6 to 9 (local time), showcasing high-torque-density drive technologies.
Faraday Dynamics develops next-generation servo motors and robot actuators to realize a future in which humans and robots can interact safely.

The company highlights core technologies that deliver torque performance improved by up to 217 percent over previous top-tier benchmarks, along with globally competitive torque density and continuous torque output. Through years of research and proprietary design and manufacturing capabilities, Faraday Dynamics achieves industrial value by simultaneously advancing miniaturization and weight reduction of robot actuators, lowering costs, and improving battery efficiency.

To date, Faraday Dynamics has accumulated tangible business results and technical validation references primarily in the domestic market by developing high-performance servo motors and actuators for next-generation robots. In particular, collaboration with major Korean robotics companies has led to verified applications of the FD-Series servo motors in humanoid, wearable, and collaborative robots. Based on these domestic references, the company has secured volume contracts approaching mass-production scale.

In overseas markets, Faraday Dynamics conducts technical meetings, prototype evaluations, and joint validation projects with robotics companies in the United States, Japan, and Europe. With some customers, it is carrying out phased verification procedures with export in mind. The company continues to expand global touchpoints through international exhibitions, including CES, to build a foundation for exports.

At this year’s CES, Faraday Dynamics introduced its high-torque-density drive technologies to the global market. The FD-Series servo motors serve as high-performance drive solutions for next-generation robots, including humanoid, collaborative, and wearable robots. With high torque density and superior stability in human–robot interaction, the series sets a new benchmark for robotic joint actuation.

body.cap: FD-Series servo motors displayed by Faraday Dynamics. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: The FD-Series QDD (Quasi-Direct Drive) servo motors achieve compact size and reduced weight through a structural design that maximizes internal space utilization and optimized housing. They incorporate Faraday Dynamics’ proprietary low-friction special-gear-tooth technology, minimizing mechanical losses. As a result, the motors deliver both smooth, natural motion and stable torque output required for robotic joints. Built on in-house production technologies, the motors support a wide range of diameters and gear ratios, enabling customized designs for applications ranging from small robots to large industrial robots.

The FD-Series DD (Direct Drive) servo motors feature a gearless, direct-coupled design that delivers outstanding torque performance and high backdrivability. The absence of gears reduces frictional losses and torque ripple, enabling smooth, compliant motion. Structural simplicity also enhances reliability and durability while making maintenance easier. Available in various combinations of outer diameter and height, the motors allow customers to select optimal specifications according to application size, weight, and performance requirements.

Notably, Faraday Dynamics supports rapid, custom motor production tailored to customer needs, leveraging facilities and technological capabilities that enable the company to perform more than 90 percent of the production process in-house.

A company representative said, “The FD-Series servo motors are next-generation drive solutions that simultaneously satisfy high torque, low friction, and high back-drivability. They can serve as a core actuator platform for the Physical AI era, in which robots interact safely with humans.”

Faraday Dynamics currently exports frameless motors to a humanoid robot platform company in the United States, where the products are applied as key components for robot joint actuation and are undergoing sample and performance verification. Through this process, the company validates product performance, reliability, and applicability.

body.cap: FD-Series servo motors on display by Faraday Dynamics. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Based on these verification results, discussions are underway to transition certain models to mass production following sample validation, with plans to begin mass production this summer. After establishing a mass-production system, the company aims to expand a stable supply within the U.S. market and gradually increase export volumes.

Looking ahead, Faraday Dynamics plans to leverage export achievements and technical references secured in the U.S. market to expand its business across the broader field of next-generation robotics, including humanoid robots, and to pursue sustained export growth in the global robotics market.

The company also announced plans to establish a standard product lineup of QDD-based servo modules and frameless motors, building trust through repeated technical validation and case studies of overseas applications.

Faraday Dynamics stated, “Going forward, we aim to position ourselves as a human-centered core actuator technology company for robots that physically interact with people, and to contribute to building the foundation of the next-generation Physical AI robotics ecosystem.”

The HUMANOID M.AX Alliance is a public-private consultative body formed in April 2025 with the participation of 260 organizations and companies, including AI research institutes, robot manufacturers, component suppliers, and universities and research institutions. The alliance jointly promotes the demonstration and commercialization of AI-based humanoids in industrial environments. At CES 2026, the HUMANOID M.AX Alliance Pavilion went beyond simple product displays and presented a practical model for ecosystem building by connecting AI, platform, and component technologies.
